name: The SOUQ Pampanga
description: A garden-like warehouse dinner spot in San Fernando.
longDescription: The SOUQ Pampanga is set in a large warehouse in San Fernando, dressed up with rustic furniture, hanging plants, and warm lighting. Fire-baked pizza and seafood paella are the dishes guides point first-timers to. There is a private parking lot at the entrance, and sunset is a good time to arrive, when daylight gives way to string lights.
featuredDesc: A rustic warehouse turned dinner spot, known for fire-baked pizza and seafood paella.

name: Bale Dutung
address: Paul Ave, Villa Gloria Subdivision, Angeles City, Pampanga
description: Chef Claude Tayag's home, opened for tasting menus.
longDescription: Bale Dutung, meaning "House of Wood", is chef Claude Tayag's own home in Angeles City, opened for pre-arranged Kapampangan meals. Reservations are needed months ahead, and the 10-course meal takes about four hours. The best-known set is the Anthony Bourdain menu, built around the dishes the late chef ate on his visit, and a lechon menu is also on offer. The house sits inside a quiet residential village, so parking is easy.

name: Mila's Tokwa't Baboy
address: San Angelo St, Brgy. San Roque, Angeles City, Pampanga
description: No-frills sisig and tokwa't baboy in Angeles.
longDescription: Mila's began as a small neighborhood stall and grew into a local institution in Angeles City. The kitchen fries its own take on sisig and serves it on a hot sizzling plate, but the dish most people come for is tokwa't baboy: fried tofu and boiled pork ears in a soy-vinegar dressing. Service is casual. Find a table, order a soda, and eat. Tripadvisor reviewers also mention crispy ulo, pata, dinuguan, and street-style barbecue.

name: Abe's Farm
address: 98 Livestock Village, Barangay Ayala, Magalang, Pampanga
description: Kapampangan cooking at the foot of Mount Arayat.
longDescription: Abe's Farm is worth the drive out to Magalang, at the foothills of Mount Arayat. Meals are served in a traditional wooden hut surrounded by greenery. Guides recommend the bamboo rice and the sinigang na baboy sa ube, a sour pork soup thickened with purple yam. The menu also includes spicy sizzling sisig, crispy tadyang, and adventurous dishes such as farm crickets. Stay for a cup of local coffee afterwards.

name: Matam-ih Authentic Kapampangan Cuisine
address: Manuel A. Roxas Hwy, Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga
longDescription: Matam-ih has a very large open-air dining area inside the Clark Freeport Zone. Staff wear traditional Aeta clothing and dishes carry indigenous names. Start with the binulo na tinola, a chicken soup cooked inside a bamboo stalk. The menu also leans into exotic and gamey meats, which makes it a good stop for a group that wants a crash course in Kapampangan food. The parking lot is large.
featuredDesc: A big open-air Kapampangan restaurant in Clark, known for bamboo-cooked chicken soup.
